skill.name: moodle-external-api-development
skill.description: Guides development of Moodle external web service APIs with parameter schemas, permissions, database access, registration, testing, and troubleshooting patterns.
skill.summary: Build structured Moodle REST and AJAX endpoints using the external API framework.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 109 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, fixed Moodle examples, placeholder endpoints, or official documentation links. Semantic review found a high-severity authorization omission plus medium-severity logging and credential-handling risks in the guidance.

remediation.issue: The quiz-attempt example reads data for supplied users without authorization checks.
remediation.suggestion: Assign validated parameters, validate the course context, and require a suitable capability before querying user attempt data.

remediation.issue: The debug logger uses mode 0777 and stores sensitive operational details.
remediation.suggestion: Use Moodle logging APIs, restrictive permissions, redaction, retention limits, and production-safe messages without SQL or stack traces.

remediation.issue: The curl examples expose passwords and tokens as command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use a protected input file or environment-specific secret mechanism, avoid administrator credentials, and warn users about shell history.

semantic_findings.title: Read Endpoint Omits Authorization Checks
semantic_findings.description: The final quiz-attempt endpoint accepts arbitrary user and course identifiers but does not validate context or require a capability before reading records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete method body validates parameter shape only, then queries another user by supplied identifiers without any context or capability check.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Debug Data Written to Permissive Logs
semantic_findings.description: The logging example creates a world-writable directory and records identifiers, SQL, exception messages, and stack traces, increasing disclosure and tampering risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly uses mode 0777 and writes request identifiers, the last SQL statement, exception details, and full stack traces.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Exposed Through Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The curl examples place an administrator password and web-service token in command arguments, which can remain in shell history or process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples pass password and token values through repeated command-line data arguments, a known local credential exposure path.

content.value_statement: Custom Moodle web services are easy to expose incorrectly or structure inconsistently. This skill provides patterns for parameters, permissions, registration, database access, testing, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains the three-method Moodle external API structure.
Shows parameter and return schemas for simple and nested values.
Demonstrates context validation, capability checks, and parameterized queries.
Covers service registration for REST and AJAX access.
Provides testing, transaction, course module, group, and troubleshooting patterns.
limitations: Examples use placeholders and require adaptation to each plugin and Moodle version.
The skill does not inspect a live Moodle installation or execute tests.
Some examples need stronger authorization, logging, and credential handling before production use.
The referenced comprehensive quiz creation file is not included.

use_cases.title: Create a Plugin Endpoint
use_cases.description: Draft a Moodle external function with validated parameters, permissions, return definitions, and service registration.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Service
use_cases.description: Check an endpoint for framework structure, database safety, permission enforcement, and response consistency.

use_cases.title: Connect an External Client
use_cases.description: Plan REST or AJAX access, token usage, testing steps, and expected Moodle configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Read Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-only Moodle endpoint for [resource]. Include parameter definitions, context validation, capability checks, return structure, and service registration.

prompt_templates.title: Review Endpoint Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Moodle endpoint for validation, context, capabilities, SQL safety, return accuracy, and information disclosure. Explain each required change.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Write Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a transactional Moodle API that creates [activity]. Include rollback behavior, capability checks, idempotency decisions, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Threat Model API Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare REST and AJAX exposure for this Moodle function. Cover tokens, authorization, sensitive logging, rate limits, and failure responses.

output_examples.input: Create a read endpoint for course progress.
output_examples.output: A file-by-file implementation outline with parameter definitions, course context checks, required capabilities, response fields, and service registration.

output_examples.input: Review a quiz-attempt endpoint for security.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review identifying missing authorization, unsafe diagnostics, query concerns, and focused remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan testing for a Moodle write service.
output_examples.output: A test matrix covering roles, invalid parameters, denied access, transaction rollback, duplicate requests, and return-schema validation.

best_practices: Validate parameters, context, and capabilities inside every endpoint.
Use parameterized Moodle database methods and short transactions.
Test authorized and unauthorized roles with production-safe logging enabled.
anti_patterns: Do not trust a user identifier merely because it passed type validation.
Do not log tokens, full SQL statements, or stack traces in production.
Do not expose write functions without explicit capabilities and rollback tests.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete Moodle plugin?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns and file guidance, but plugin metadata, language strings, capabilities, and tests still require project-specific work.

faq.question: Which Moodle API methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers execute_parameters, execute, execute_returns, service registration, database access, transactions, REST testing, and AJAX calls.

faq.question: Does it support both read and write endpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains read and write registration and includes transaction and course activity patterns for write operations.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Adapt them to your Moodle version and add complete authorization, secure logging, credential protection, and automated tests.

faq.question: Can it test my Moodle installation?
faq.answer: No. It provides test procedures and review guidance but cannot access or validate a live installation by itself.

faq.question: How should API permissions be enforced?
faq.answer: Validate the relevant context and require specific capabilities inside each function before reading or changing protected data.
